```
1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	image_processor.py
4	
5	Resizes images to 4800px on the long side and applies a centered
6	'lucid_world' watermark. Reads from Input_Images/, writes to Processed_Images/.
7	"""
8	
9	from pathlib import Path
10	from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
11	
12	# ── Config ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
13	LONG_SIDE = 4800
14	WATERMARK_TEXT = "lucid_world"
15	WATERMARK_COLOR = (255, 255, 255, 140)   # white, ~55% opacity
16	FONT_PATH = "/System/Library/Fonts/Helvetica.ttc"
17	SUPPORTED_EXTS = {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".tif", ".tiff", ".webp"}
18	
19	BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).parent
20	INPUT_DIR = BASE_DIR / "Input_Images"
21	OUTPUT_DIR = BASE_DIR / "Processed_Images"
22	WATERMARK_DIR = OUTPUT_DIR / "Watermarked_Images"
23	RESIZED_DIR = OUTPUT_DIR / "Resized_Images"
24	
25	
26	def resize_to_long_side(img: Image.Image, long_side: int) -> Image.Image:
27	    w, h = img.size
28	    if w >= h:
29	        new_w = long_side
30	        new_h = round(h * long_side / w)
31	    else:
32	        new_h = long_side
33	        new_w = round(w * long_side / h)
34	    return img.resize((new_w, new_h), Image.LANCZOS)
35	
36	
37	def add_watermark(img: Image.Image) -> Image.Image:
38	    base = img.convert("RGBA")
39	    W, H = base.size
40	
41	    # Render at a large size first, then scale to fit width
42	    working_font_size = max(200, H // 4)
43	    try:
44	        font = ImageFont.truetype(FONT_PATH, working_font_size)
45	    except OSError:
46	        print(f"  [warn] Could not load {FONT_PATH}, falling back to default font.")
47	        font = ImageFont.load_default()
48	
49	    tmp_draw = ImageDraw.Draw(Image.new("RGBA", (1, 1)))
50	    bbox = tmp_draw.textbbox((0, 0), WATERMARK_TEXT, font=font)
51	    text_w = bbox[2] - bbox[0]
52	    text_h = bbox[3] - bbox[1]
53	
54	    # Render text onto its own canvas
55	    txt_img = Image.new("RGBA", (text_w + 20, text_h + 20), (0, 0, 0, 0))
56	    txt_draw = ImageDraw.Draw(txt_img)
57	    txt_draw.text((-bbox[0] + 10, -bbox[1] + 10), WATERMARK_TEXT,
58	                  font=font, fill=WATERMARK_COLOR)
59	
60	    # Scale so text spans 90% of image width, horizontally
61	    target_w = round(W * 0.90)
62	    scale = target_w / txt_img.width
63	    new_w = target_w
64	    new_h = round(txt_img.height * scale)
65	    txt_img = txt_img.resize((new_w, new_h), Image.LANCZOS)
66	
67	    # Centre horizontally and vertically
68	    paste_x = (W - new_w) // 2
69	    paste_y = (H - new_h) // 2
70	
71	    overlay = Image.new("RGBA", base.size, (0, 0, 0, 0))
72	    overlay.paste(txt_img, (paste_x, paste_y), txt_img)
73	
74	    return Image.alpha_composite(base, overlay)
75	
76	
77	def save_img(img: Image.Image, out_path: Path, ext: str):
78	    if ext in {".jpg", ".jpeg"}:
79	        img.convert("RGB").save(out_path, "JPEG", quality=92, optimize=True)
80	    else:
81	        img.save(out_path, optimize=True)
82	
83	
84	def process_images():
85	    INPUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
86	    OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
87	    WATERMARK_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
88	    RESIZED_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
89	
90	    images = [p for p in INPUT_DIR.iterdir() if p.suffix.lower() in SUPPORTED_EXTS]
91	
92	    if not images:
93	        print(f"No images found in {INPUT_DIR}/")
94	        print("Drop your images there and run the script again.")
95	        return
96	
97	    print(f"Found {len(images)} image(s) — processing...\n")
98	
99	    for src_path in sorted(images):
100	        ext = src_path.suffix.lower()
101	
102	        with Image.open(src_path) as img:
103	            img.load()
104	
105	            # ── 1. Watermark only ──
106	            watermarked = add_watermark(img.copy())
107	            wm_path = WATERMARK_DIR / (src_path.stem + "_watermarked" + src_path.suffix)
108	            save_img(watermarked, wm_path, ext)
109	            print(f"  [watermark] {src_path.name}  →  {wm_path.name}  ✓")
110	
111	            # ── 2. Resize / upscale to 4800 long side ──
112	            resized = resize_to_long_side(img.copy(), LONG_SIDE)
113	            rs_path = RESIZED_DIR / (src_path.stem + "_resized" + src_path.suffix)
114	            save_img(resized.convert("RGB") if ext in {".jpg", ".jpeg"} else resized, rs_path, ext)
115	            print(f"  [resize]    {src_path.name}  →  {rs_path.name}  ✓\n")
116	
117	    print(f"Watermarked → {WATERMARK_DIR}/")
118	    print(f"Resized     → {RESIZED_DIR}/")
119	
120	    import subprocess
121	    subprocess.run(["open", str(OUTPUT_DIR)])
122	
123	
124	if __name__ == "__main__":
125	    process_images()
126
```

```json
  "command": "ffmpeg -i \"/Users/carlosrestrepo/Movies/CapCut/Surreal humanoid figure.mov\" \\\n  -filter_complex \"[0:v]split[v1][v2];[v2]reverse[vr];[v1][vr]concat=n=2:v=1:a=0[outv]\" \\\n  -map \"[outv]\" -c:v libx264 -crf 18 -preset slow -pix_fmt yuv420p \\\n  \"$HOME/Desktop/Surreal_Humanoid_Loop.mp4\" -y 2>&1 | tail -3 && \\\n  ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of default=noprint_wrappers=1 \"$HOME/Desktop/Surreal_Humanoid_Loop.mp4\"",

}
```

```json
{
  "command": "python3 << 'EOF'\nfrom PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nFONT_PATH = \"/System/Library/Fonts/Helvetica.ttc\"\nWATERMARK_TEXT = \"lucid_world\"\nWATERMARK_COLOR = (255, 255, 255, 140)\n\ndef add_watermark(img):\n    base = img.convert(\"RGBA\")\n    W, H = base.size\n    working_font_size = max(200, H // 4)\n    font = ImageFont.truetype(FONT_PATH, working_font_size)\n    tmp_draw = ImageDraw.Draw(Image.new(\"RGBA\", (1, 1)))\n    bbox = tmp_draw.textbbox((0, 0), WATERMARK_TEXT, font=font)\n    text_w, text_h = bbox[2] - bbox[0], bbox[3] - bbox[1]\n    txt_img = Image.new(\"RGBA\", (text_w + 20, text_h + 20), (0, 0, 0, 0))\n    txt_draw = ImageDraw.Draw(txt_img)\n    txt_draw.text((-bbox[0] + 10, -bbox[1] + 10), WATERMARK_TEXT, font=font, fill=WATERMARK_COLOR)\n    target_w = round(W * 0.80)\n    scale = target_w / txt_img.width\n    txt_img = txt_img.resize((target_w, round(txt_img.height * scale)), Image.LANCZOS)\n    paste_x = (W - txt_img.width) // 2\n    paste_y = (H - txt_img.height) // 2\n    overlay = Image.new(\"RGBA\", base.size, (0, 0, 0, 0))\n    overlay.paste(txt_img, (paste_x, paste_y), txt_img)\n    return Image.alpha_composite(base, overlay)\n\n# 1. Watermarked thumbnail\nimg = Image.open(\"/tmp/thumbnail_raw.png\")\nimg = img.resize((1920, 1080), Image.LANCZOS)\nwatermarked = add_watermark(img)\nwatermarked.convert(\"RGB\").save(\"/Users/carlosrestrepo/Desktop/listing_thumbnail.jpg\", \"JPEG\", quality=92)\nprint(\"Thumbnail saved\")\nEOF",
  "description": "Create watermarked thumbnail with PIL"
}
```

```json
{
  "command": "# Create low-res (720p) preview clip from the looping MP4, then burn watermark via overlay using Python on each frame\n# Easier: extract frames, watermark, reassemble — but for a 9s clip that's slow.\n# Better: use ffmpeg to scale down to 720p first, then overlay a watermark image\n\n# First create a semi-transparent watermark PNG with PIL\npython3 << 'EOF'\nfrom PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont\n\nFONT_PATH = \"/System/Library/Fonts/Helvetica.ttc\"\nW, H = 1280, 720\nfont = ImageFont.truetype(FONT_PATH, 160)\ntmp_draw = ImageDraw.Draw(Image.new(\"RGBA\", (1, 1)))\nbbox = tmp_draw.textbbox((0, 0), \"lucid_world\", font=font)\ntext_w, text_h = bbox[2]-bbox[0], bbox[3]-bbox[1]\ntxt_img = Image.new(\"RGBA\", (text_w+20, text_h+20), (0,0,0,0))\ntxt_draw = ImageDraw.Draw(txt_img)\ntxt_draw.text((-bbox[0]+10, -bbox[1]+10), \"lucid_world\", font=font, fill=(255,255,255,140))\ntarget_w = round(W * 0.80)\nscale = target_w / txt_img.width\ntxt_img = txt_img.resize((target_w, round(txt_img.height * scale)), Image.LANCZOS)\nwm = Image.new(\"RGBA\", (W, H), (0,0,0,0))\npaste_x = (W - txt_img.width) // 2\npaste_y = (H - txt_img.height) // 2\nwm.paste(txt_img, (paste_x, paste_y), txt_img)\nwm.save(\"/tmp/wm_overlay.png\")\nprint(\"Watermark overlay saved\")\nEOF",
  "description": "Create watermark overlay PNG for video"
}
```

rcap the process we did for the video loop

> AGENT

Here's the full process we used:

**1. Check the source file**
```bash
ffprobe
```
Got info: 9 sec, 4K (3872×2160), 30fps, H.264 .mov

**2. First attempt (failed)**
Used `ffmpeg concat` with a separate reversed clip → created a 462-minute file with bad metadata

**3. Fixed with filter_complex**
```bash
ffmpeg -i "source.mov" \
  -filter_complex "[0:v]split[v1][v2];[v2]reverse[vr];[v1][vr]concat=n=2:v=1:a=0[outv]" \
  -map "[outv]" -c:v libx264 -crf 18 -preset slow -pix_fmt yuv420p \
  output.mp4
```
Result: 18-second seamless boomerang loop (forward + reverse)

**4. Watermarked thumbnail**
Used PIL to extract frame at 4s → resize to 1920×1080 → add `lucid_world` watermark

**5. Watermarked preview clip**
- Created a transparent PNG watermark overlay with PIL
- Used ffmpeg `overlay` filter to burn it onto a 720p downscaled version of the loop

**Key lesson:** Use `filter_complex` for reverse+concat — the concat demuxer method creates corrupt duration metadata.

```
---
name: banana-image-prompts
description: >
  Image prompt generator for Banana (Gemini) image generation models — Banana Nano, Banana Pro, and Banana Nano 2. Use this skill whenever the user wants to generate, write, or improve an image prompt for Banana, Gemini image generation, or any AI image generator. Triggers on: "write a prompt", "image prompt", "generate a prompt for", "banana prompt", "make a prompt for my image", "help me prompt", "create an image of", or any request to generate visual content through an AI image tool. Even if the user just describes a scene or subject and says "make me an image" or "generate this", use this skill immediately to craft the best possible prompt for them.
---

# Banana Image Prompt Generator

You are a specialized image prompt engineer for Banana (Google Gemini) image generation models. Your job is to transform any idea — no matter how simple or vague — into a rich, detailed, cinematic prompt that coaxes the most beautiful, photorealistic, and artistically compelling image possible from the model.

Think like a seasoned photographer, cinematographer, and visual artist rolled into one. Every prompt you write should feel like a shot list from a film director combined with the vision of a fine art photographer.

---

## Model Awareness

Tailor prompt complexity to the model being used:

**Banana Nano** (Gemini Flash Image — fast, lighter model)
- Keep prompts focused and punchy — 2-4 sentences
- Lean on strong, clear visual anchors
- Avoid overly layered or complex scene descriptions
- Great for: quick iterations, character consistency, creative experiments

**Banana Pro** (Gemini Pro Image — studio-quality, reasoning-capable)
- Go long and rich — 5-8 sentences
- Layer in fine detail: texture, micro-expressions, atmosphere, post-processing style
- Supports complex compositions, text elements, multi-subject scenes
- Great for: final outputs, commercial quality, high-detail realism
```
